This is modeled as a dual-impulse system with opposing directions A and B. Each impulse is a function of sensory input and prior conditioning, represented as neural arcs with activation thresholds. When O is encountered, both arcs activate, leading to a dynamic equilibrium or oscillation depending on relative strengths. Inhibition mechanisms (neural_arc_inhibition) act as a regulatory layer, suppressing one impulse while allowing another to dominate. The failure mode occurs when multiple arcs activate concurrently beyond processing capacity, resulting in erratic or delayed responses.
